events.title: Newton's Principia Is Published
events.description: Isaac Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica was first published, setting out his three laws of motion and his law of universal gravitation.
events.significance: The book laid the foundations of classical mechanics. It shaped physics and astronomy for more than two centuries.

events.title: Venezuela Declares Independence from Spain
events.description: Seven Venezuelan provinces declared independence from Spain, one of the earliest such declarations in Spanish South America.
events.significance: The declaration helped set off the wider struggle for independence across Latin America. Venezuela still marks July 5 as its Independence Day.

events.title: Algiers Surrenders to French Forces
events.description: Algiers surrendered to the invading French, which ended the Regency of Algiers, the Ottoman-era state that had governed the region for centuries.
events.significance: It began roughly 132 years of French rule in Algeria. Algeria's independence in 1962 came on the same calendar date.

events.title: Thomas Cook Launches Organized Travel
events.description: Thomas Cook ran his first organized excursion in England and went on to build a travel business around it.
events.significance: The venture is widely seen as the start of the modern travel industry and package tourism.

events.title: Task Force Smith Fights at Osan
events.description: In the first ground clash of the Korean War between American and North Korean forces, the Battle of Osan routed a small U.S. Army task force.
events.significance: The battle showed how unprepared U.S. forces were. It also marked the start of a major American ground commitment in Korea.
